title: Fees printed for two or more years
question: Where the same fee is printed for more than one year, how much did it change?
finding: Building Inspection's hourly inspection rate was $158.10 before the 2023 fee ordinance, which wrote in $181.82; the 2024 ordinance struck that out and wrote in $461 (+154%); the table effective July 12, 2026 prints $519, 3.3 times the figure of three years earlier. The hourly plan review rate went from $173.91 to $526 over the same ordinances. 59 Planning application fees are printed for two years and rise by a middle figure of +2.4% from August 29, 2025 to August 31, 2026, the yearly cost-of-living adjustment the schedule describes. 54 development impact fee lines that could be followed through five or more yearly registers rose by a middle figure of +24% from first to last. Most other fees are published for the current year only.
how: Building Inspection: lines of the 2023 and 2024 fee ordinances where the scan shows the old and new amounts side by side, set against each other and against the 2026 table. Planning: a printed line is matched between the two schedules when its wording, with the amount removed, is identical and occurs once in each. Impact fees: the same test across the yearly registers, kept only where the line appears in five or more years and never falls (a guard against columns being mis-joined; 4 lines failed it and are left out).
limits: The Planning schedule states that fees are adjusted each year by the consumer price index. The ordinance is a scanned document: struck-out and inserted amounts are run together in its text layer and were separated by rule, so check the linked original. Impact-fee lines are wrapped multi-column table rows; the matched line is quoted but its label can be incomplete. Building Inspection, Public Works, Fire and Health post only their current tables, so their history is missing; the two fee ordinances fill part of the gap for Building Inspection.
